scenes.heading: Solubility and precipitation
scenes.sub: Mix two clear solutions... and a solid appears!
scenes.say: Mix two clear solutions, and suddenly a cloudy solid appears. That's a precipitation reaction. Chemists use them to clean wastewater and identify ions. Let's learn to predict them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Fans mob a team huddle and pull players out one by one
scenes.science: Water molecules pull ions out of the lattice and surround them
scenes.breaks: if the lattice holds too tightly, like silver chloride, it's insoluble, though a tiny amount still dissolves.
scenes.say: Picture a footy team in a tight huddle after the siren. The players are ions in a lattice. Fans rush on and pull players out one by one. In water, the fans are polar water molecules. If their pull beats the attractions in the lattice, the ions separate and end up surrounded by water.

scenes.heading: Two ways to dissolve
scenes.say: Ionic compounds like salt split into ions when they dissolve, so the solution conducts. Polar molecules like glucose dissolve whole, by hydrogen bonding with water, so the solution doesn't conduct.

scenes.heading: Solubility rules
scenes.say: Use the solubility table. Nitrates, ethanoates, group one ions and ammonium are always soluble. Chlorides, bromides and iodides are soluble, except with silver and lead, the troublemakers. Most sulfates are soluble, except barium, lead, and calcium slightly.

scenes.heading: Predicting a precipitate
steps: Check each new pair in the table
scenes.say: To predict a precipitate, write the ions, then swap partners like at a dance. Check each new pair in the solubility table. If one is insoluble, it falls out as a precipitate.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide solutions are mixed. What forms? Write the net ionic equation.
scenes.say: Mix lead nitrate and potassium iodide. Swap partners to get lead iodide and potassium nitrate. Iodides are insoluble with lead, so a yellow precipitate of lead iodide forms. Potassium and nitrate are spectator ions, like the crowd at a game. Cross them out to get the net ionic equation.

scenes.heading: Solubility curves
points: Most solids: more soluble when hot
scenes.say: A solubility curve shows how much dissolves at each temperature. On the curve is saturated; below it is unsaturated. Most solids dissolve better when hot, but gases are the opposite, so warm water holds less oxygen.

points: Ag⁺ and Pb²⁺ are the troublemakers
Net ionic: leave out spectator ions
scenes.say: Quick recap. Ionic compounds dissociate into ions. Silver and lead are the troublemakers. To predict a precipitate, swap partners and check the table. And the net ionic equation leaves out spectator ions. Now try the practice questions!
